title: Blood cancer clinical trials long-term follow-up using integrated Healthcare Systems Data
official: A data linkage study integrating randomised clinical trials with national Healthcare Systems Data
summary:
Background and study aims
Clinical trials play an important role in finding better treatments for blood cancers. However, many trials rely on regular hospital visits and special trial paperwork to follow patients over many years. This can be tiring for patients, takes a lot of time for doctors and nurses, and can be expensive to manage.  This is especially true for conditions like multiple myeloma, where people may live for many years after joining a trial. At the same time, the NHS already routinely collects information about hospital visits and deaths as part of everyday care (this is called healthcare systems data),  but we do not yet know how well this information works in blood cancer trials.
The BLISS study will link data we already hold at the Clinical Trials Research Unit (CTRU) in Leeds with healthcare systems data from NHS England.  We're only looking at the data from 10 clinical trials which were run at the CTRU and all of these trials have now closed.  We will  use the information we receive from NHS England to answer information research questions, such as:
1. Whether treatments have had a long-term benefit
2. How frailty is assessed
3. How bone disease is treated
4. If trials represent all patients who get blood cancers

Who can participate?
The study involves participants who consented to take place in one or more of the completed clinical trials which were run at the Leeds CTRU between 2008 and 2021: Myeloma X, MUKOne, MUKFour, MUKSix, MUKEight, Myeloma XI, MUKThree, MUK Five, MUKSeven, or MUKTwelve.
At the time these trials took place, we did not ask for consent for linkage to data records held by national providers (such as a NHS England).  As these trials have now closed and some people may have moved away,  it is not possible to contact everyone.  We have therefore obtained permission to obtain follow up data  from the Health Research Authority (who take advice from the Confidentiality Advisory Group).  This involves sharing a limited amount of personal data (NHS Number, date of birth and sex) with NHS England to obtain linked healthcare systems data.
If you took part in one of these trials and are happy to be included in the study, you do not need to do anything.  If you took part in one of these trials and do not wish to be included in the study, you can opt out by visiting https://ctru.leeds.ac.uk/bliss/ or contacting a member of the BLISS team.  
Any person who took part in one of these trials and withdrew their consent from further data collection will not be included in the BLISS study.  After the data linkage has occurred, a persons data is de identified and researchers will not be able to see identifiable data.
 
What does the study involve?
In this study, we are bringing together information from several UK multiple myeloma clinical trials with existing NHS records, such as national death registrations, cancer records, and hospital admissions. We will carefully compare the information collected during the trials with NHS records to see how accurate and complete the routine data are. In particular, we want to understand whether NHS death records can be reliably used to track long term survival, instead of relying solely on trial follow up visits.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
This research could help to answer important research questions about myeloma more quickly.  It could do this by  making it easier to follow people for longer periods and improve our understanding of long-term outcomes in blood cancer.  It can also help to make future trials simpler and less demanding for patients by reducing the need for extra hospital appointments and paperwork. Overall, this approach could help make clinical research more efficient, more patient‑friendly, and still produce high quality information to improve care.

Where is the study run from?
University of Leeds (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
February 2026 to April 2030 

Who is funding the study?
Blood Cancer UK (BCUK)

Who is the main contact?
Lesley Smith/Sharon Gillson, Ctru-bliss@leeds.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participants must have taken part in at least one of the  completed multiple myeloma clinical trials conducted by the University of Leeds CTRU between 2008 and 2021 as per below:
1.1. MUKOne: ISRCTN90889843
1.2. MUKThree: ISRCTN24989786
1.3. MUKFour: ISRCTN08577602
1.4. MUKFive: ISRCTN17354232
1.5. MUKSix: ISRCTN59395590
1.6. MUKSeven: ISRCTN24593488
1.7. MUKEight: ISRCTN58227268
1.8. MUKTwelve: ISRCTN15028850
1.9. Myeloma X: ISRCTN60123120
1.10. Myeloma XI: ISRCTN49407852
2. Participants must have been recruited to one or more of the listed clinical trials at a trial location based in England
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participants who have withdrawn from further data collection from any of the listed multiple myeloma clinical trials 
2. Participants recruited to a trial location (involved in one more of the listed clinical trials) outside of England
3. Participants who have opted out of the data linkage study
